question: In order to study at university students are required to pay expensive tuition fees Not all student can afford them so some people think that university education should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Education is a necessary step in pursuing one’s dream and passion. Whether you wich to be a musicican or an engineer, being in an environment that allows you to attain the knowledge needed, as well as surround yourself with like-minded people is instrumental in getting that wish. However, in many cases, students don’t have this privilege. Some people believe that universities should be free so students can get the education they want; however, I think that that would lower the qualities of the education and that instead, tuition should just be lowered to a reasonable amount. 

To begin with, universities are costly. It’s not cheap at all to run such large-scale facilities, consdering they typically house up to thousands of students. Not to mention, if universities are made free, significantly more people would enroll, making maintenance even more costly. Besides the dozens of staffs needed to run it, a large group of professors are there to teach the students too. To most of them, this is their main source of income; and so, if universities are made free, how will these staffs feed themselves and their families? Arguments could be made about how universities could receive their funds from companies, governments and donations. However, these are too inconsistent to be reliable. Companies funds and donations might not be enough considering the amount of universities there is. Moreover, universities being fully government funded will heavily increase tax money, which many people will be against. Overall, there exists a lot of downsides to eliminating tuition money. 

A better solution would be to aid students through othermeans. While company funds and donations alone might not be enough to alleviate the pressure of money, it could help enough so that universities could lower their tuition money to a reasonable amount. Furthermore, they could have programs for less fortunate students. For example, if a student can register that they are from a financially disadvantaged background, they could be exempt from paying tuition. Moreover, scholarships can be handed to students who display hardwork and high achievements. This way, those who work hard would be more encouraged and supported, and the universities’ quality would not be compromised. 

In conclusion, while making univerities free sound like a good decision, it is currently not possible to pursue. Instead the best option is to encourage students who work hard and simply lowering tuition.
